actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/npm.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/npm.purpose: Inspect packages or publish a declared package through npm.

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@cli/shell.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/shell.note: Resolve to the session shell (PowerShell, bash or another declared shell); do not assume bash on Windows. Arguments remain separate data until encoded for that shell.
@cli/shell.purpose: Run a declared command in the active session shell.

@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

claude.via: Claude Code Read, Glob and Grep

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces/artifacts.purpose: Produced files, including images, documents and other deliverables.

@workspaces/context.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/context.purpose: Supporting reference files for a request.

@workspaces/fe.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/fe.purpose: The explicitly bound frontend checkout; unavailable when the project has no frontend role.

@workspaces/inputs.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/inputs.purpose: Files supplied as the subject of a request.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/responses.purpose: Responses declaring produced outputs and execution status.

Before retrying an uncertain publication, observe @remote/npm by package version and integrity; the feedback budget grants no duplicate write.

criteria.stopWhen: Return done only when criteriaResults accepts every review applicable to the selected mode and all machine criteria pass. Stop after two feedback rounds or an unchanged repeated failure; uncertain publication blocks until observed.

purpose: Repair one explicitly authorized owner package, prove the paired regression, create a reproducible release, and optionally publish or consume that exact release within declared boundaries.

request.description: inputs.prompts select owner, consumer or end-to-end mode and publication intent; name package identity, exact owner and consumer file ceilings, paired regression, unchanged commands, next patch version and registry. inputs.files carry the plans and any bound release archive. context files carry UI-family authority when relevant.
request.title: library.update request

response.description: A done response contains at least the mode's local change commit, exact release record and raw proof report. End-to-end mode may include separate owner and consumer commits; publication evidence is recorded only when requested and observed.
response.title: library.update response

scope: The request selects owner, consumer or end-to-end mode. Owner mode changes only declared package behavior, paired tests and patch-version metadata. Consumer mode changes only named dependency metadata. Publication targets the package manifest registry. No push, merge, tag, deployment or unrelated dependency change is allowed.

calls.purpose: Read exact package, plan, release and consumer bindings.
Verify the frozen local bases and clean declared paths.

steps.instruction: Read the selected mode, package manifest, owner and consumer plans, bound release, UI-family context and exact commands. Freeze package identity, file ceilings, paired regression, next patch version, registry and publication intent before mutation. Ask for a missing plan or archive.
produces: A frozen owner and consumer boundary for the selected mode.

reads.when: for each plan or release input

calls.purpose: Write only declared owner behavior, regression and patch metadata.
Run the unchanged regression and complete package gates.
Measure and create one local owner commit.

steps.instruction: For owner or end-to-end mode, write only the paired regression and prove it fails on the base. Repair declared behavior, bump exactly the next patch version, then run the same regression and every existing declared package test, typecheck and build command unfiltered. Commit the owner set once.

calls.purpose: Pack the owner commit and, only when explicitly requested, publish then observe the exact @remote/npm package version.

steps.instruction: Pack from the exact owner commit and record archive version, file list and integrity. If publication is requested, publish the unmodified archive to @remote/npm using the manifest registry, then read the served version and integrity back. After an uncertain call, observe the registry first; never republish blindly.

writes.when: after packing or binding a supplied release

calls.purpose: Install only the exact bound archive within declared dependency metadata.
Run unchanged consumer regression and complete gates.
Measure and create one local consumer metadata commit.

steps.instruction: For consumer or end-to-end mode, bind the exact release archive by integrity, run the unchanged baseline consumer proof, change only named dependency and lock entries, verify installed bytes match the archive, rerun the proof and every consumer gate, then commit consumer metadata once.

calls.purpose: Persist combined proof and response metadata.
Validate the compiled request and response.

steps.instruction: Inspect package and consumer diffs, raw proofs, archive and any registry observation. Give concrete feedback to the owning step, make only a targeted repair and rerun dependent proofs. Persist the combined proof report and response after all criteria accept current outputs.

validate.failurePolicy: Reproduce, repair, package, observe and reassess. Feedback returns to the owning half only. An uncertain registry publication is observed by version and integrity before any retry; duplicate publication is never authorized by the feedback budget.

review.instruction: Inspect owner changes: only declared existing behavior, paired regression, changelog and patch-version metadata may change. Reject new dependencies, scripts, unrelated public deltas and files outside the package ceiling.
Require the same regression to fail on the bound base and pass on the repair, followed by every declared unfiltered package test, typecheck and build command with raw output.

Verify the archive was packed from the owner commit, has the requested next patch version and recorded integrity, and any registry publication at @remote/npm was read back with matching version and integrity.

Inspect consumer changes: only the named dependency entries and corresponding lock entries may change. Installed package bytes must match the bound release; unrelated versions, source, tests and scripts remain unchanged.
Require the unchanged consumer regression or before/after audit plus every declared consumer gate on the exact installed release. Failed or filtered checks cannot be accepted.
